description: Answer "which eSIM should I buy for this trip?". Give it the stops, a country code and the days spent in each, and it compares one plan covering the whole route against one plan per country against a mix of the two, on live prices, then flags the cheapest option that covers everything and explains the choice in a sentence you can quote. It also estimates the data each stop needs, names any country SimFuse cannot cover, and returns package ids that go straight into create-checkout-session. Use it whenever a trip has two or more countries, and for a single country when the traveller wants a recommendation rather than a list. Read-only: nothing is reserved and nothing is charged, and the totals are today's catalog prices, not a quote held for later.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code every price is quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

start.description: Optional. Departure date as YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2026-04-18". Only used to date the stops in the answer; it does not change prices. Defaults to today.

stops.description: The trip, one entry per country, in travel order. 1 to 12 stops, e.g. [{"country":"JP","days":7},{"country":"KR","days":5}].

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. "JP" for Japan. Look one up with list-destinations rather than guessing. Each country may appear once: give one stop with the total days rather than two visits.

days.description: Days spent in that country, 1 to 365. Count the nights of the stay.

usage.description: Optional. How heavily data is used during this stop: "light" (about 300 MB a day, maps and messaging), "regular" (about 800 MB a day) or "heavy" (about 2 GB a day, video and hotspot). Overrides the trip-wide `usage` for this stop only.
Optional. Trip-wide data usage for stops that do not set their own: "light" (about 300 MB a day), "regular" (about 800 MB a day) or "heavy" (about 2 GB a day). Defaults to "regular".

name: plan-trip

checkout.description: How to act on the recommendation.

checkout_sessions.description: HTTP endpoint that opens a checkout session, if you would rather not use the create-checkout-session tool.

human_url.description: Where to send a person to buy this themselves.

items.description: The recommended option as checkout line items, ready to pass to create-checkout-session. Null when nothing covers the trip.

note.description: What the totals are and are not: catalog prices today, never a reservation.

register.description: HTTP endpoint that mints an agent key for that API.

contract.description: Version of this answer's shape. "1" today; it only changes when an existing field changes meaning.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code every amount below is quoted in, e.g. "EUR".

options.description: Every way of buying the trip that we could price, cheapest-first within each strategy. Empty when nothing we sell covers it.

complete.description: True when this option covers every stop. False means at least one stop is left without data.

esims.description: How many eSIMs the traveller installs under this option.

covers.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the stops this line covers.

data.description: Allowance written for a person, e.g. "5 GB" or "Unlimited".

data_mb.description: Allowance in megabytes. 0 on an unlimited plan, where `policy` carries the real terms.

name.description: Plan name as a traveller sees it.

package_id.description: The plan id to buy. Pass it to create-checkout-session or get-plan.

policy.description: What the plan really gives you. Null when the supplier has never published its terms, which is different from having no limits.

high_speed_data_mb.description: Full-speed allowance in megabytes PER RESET PERIOD, so 1 GB a day for 30 days is 1024, not 30720. 0 means genuinely uncapped.

max_speed_kbps.description: Speed ceiling in kbit/s from the first megabyte. Null means no ceiling.

reduced_speed_kbps.description: Speed in kbit/s after the full-speed allowance is used. Null means the data STOPS rather than slowing down.

reset_period.description: How often the full-speed allowance resets. Null means it covers the whole plan.

price.description: The same price formatted for a person.

price_cents.description: Price for one of this plan, in minor units (cents) of the response currency.

quantity.description: How many of this plan to buy.

unlimited.description: True when the plan is sold as unlimited, which almost always means unlimited up to a fair-use cap.

validity_days.description: How many days the plan stays valid once it activates.

purchasable.description: False when the option needs more eSIMs than one order can carry.

recommended.description: True on the one option this answer recommends.

saves_cents.description: What this option saves against the next cheapest complete alternative, in minor units. 0 when there is none or when it is dearer.

strategy.description: How this option buys the trip.

total.description: The same total formatted for a person, e.g. "24.50 EUR".

total_cents.description: Total price in minor units (cents) of the response currency, so 2450 is 24.50.

warnings.description: What this option does not do: a stop it leaves uncovered, a plan that runs out or expires early. Empty when there is nothing to say.

planner_url.description: The same trip on the SimFuse website, for a person who wants to finish it themselves.

reason.description: One sentence explaining the recommendation, written to be quoted to the traveller verbatim.

recommendation.description: Which strategy won: one plan for the whole route, one plan per country, or a mix. Null when nothing we sell covers the trip.

trip.description: The trip as it was understood, which is worth reading back to the traveller.

end.description: Last day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD.

span_days.description: Total days from arrival at the first stop to departure from the last.

start.description: First day of the trip, YYYY-MM-DD.

stops.description: The stops, in travel order, with their dates and data estimates.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the stop.

estimated_data.description: The same estimate written for a person, e.g. "3.9 GB".

estimated_mb.description: Data this stop is estimated to need, in megabytes (1 GB is 1024 MB).

usage.description: The data appetite used for this stop.

token.description: Compact encoding of the trip, for the planner_url link.

warnings.description: Trip-level caveats: a country SimFuse does not sell, or a gap the recommended option leaves. Say these out loud rather than dropping them.

title: Plan eSIMs for a trip
